bull.b: The sharp year-over-year improvement in revenue and net income shows that recent content launches can materially improve operating performance. If this momentum continues across the announced release schedule, it could strengthen earnings power and support reinvestment in the portfolio.

A broad forward pipeline gives Snail multiple opportunities to extend monetization beyond a single quarter and refresh player engagement over several release cycles. Continued launches across ARK, PixARK and newer franchises may diversify revenue sources and improve portfolio durability.

High unit sales and sustained daily engagement demonstrate meaningful demand for Snail's core franchise and create a base for downloadable content, updates and community-led monetization. This installed audience can support recurring commercial opportunities across future ARK releases.

bear.b: Negative equity materially reduces financial flexibility and leaves the company dependent on improving results or accessing transactions to strengthen its capital base. The weakened structure can constrain investment in games and increase the consequences of any operating setback.

Inconsistent operating and free cash flow makes it harder for Snail to fund development, marketing and live operations internally. Repeated periods of negative cash generation may increase reliance on external financing and reduce resilience when launches underperform.

Declining revenue from established titles increases the need for successful replacement content, while delaying a planned release postpones a potential source of bookings and engagement. Together, these factors can create uneven revenue progression during the transition.
